notes.1:
The motivation connects our prior static F1 comparisons to the need to update an operational IDS, then explains why TabPFN is a candidate.
Training on all attack types means the existing training data, not training on the test set. Classification itself is not inherently unsuitable for IDS; fixed-test F1 alone does not establish operational utility.
New attack labels and changing conditions motivate updates. EXP70 does not reproduce an actual network environment shift.
TabPFN does not require backbone weight retraining for context updates, but preprocessing, cache construction and inference still incur costs. This structural property is distinct from a measured cost or accuracy advantage on IDS data.
Small-data evidence: Hollmann et al., Nature 2025, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08328-6 .
Daily attack scenarios: https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/ids-2018.html and the NF-v3 timestamp validation recorded for EXP69.
notes.2:
EXP70 preserves the original order of first class appearance; it does not replay the full raw traffic chronology.
At each stage, both methods use identical cumulative labeled examples. Future classes are excluded from training, preprocessing and context until introduced.
Evaluation uses all rows of introduced classes in the existing cleaned test split. The number of evaluated classes changes across stages, so changes in overall Macro-F1 are not direct measures of improvement or forgetting.
XGBoost is retrained on cumulative data. Global TabPFN rebuilds preprocessing/cache from cumulative context with fixed backbone weights.
The final budget is 100,000 rows per dataset: 75,000 Benign plus 25,000 attack examples. Seed 43.
This experiment does not establish update behavior or cost for the full expert/S/V system.
Protocol: docs/research/20261002/exp70_protocol.md. Both methods and all stages completed for both datasets.

Completed EXP70 results: tabpfn/results/20261002_exp70_class_arrival_100k_s43/summary.csv and class_metrics.csv.

The comparison uses Global TabPFN, not the full expert/S/V system. Retention must be checked on the same existing-class examples; benign FPR alone does not establish retention of all classes.
Fit/setup is the elapsed fit_context_or_retrain phase, excluding model construction/loading. TabPFN uses a frozen backbone, CPU cache, four ensemble members and no context subsampling. Measured batch costs do not directly establish real-time service throughput.
Single seed 43 and the existing development holdout. The task is classification after labels for a new attack are supplied, not detection of unlabeled OOD attacks.
Source snapshot: docs/slides/kor/1002_operational_qa/result_snapshot.json.
CIC2018 shows higher initial F1 for Web attack and Infiltration. Overall accuracy or cost superiority across datasets is not implied. In this batch setup, XGBoost has shorter fit and inference times.

The final confusion matrix shows TabPFN MitM recall of 96.99%, precision of 2.39%, and 46,010 false positives, including 41,330 Benign rows. High recall and low precision are directly observed; the causal roles of context proportions, coverage and feature representations have not been isolated.
After adding MitM, Macro-F1 on the same existing-class test rows is 76.51% before and 76.72% after, while benign FPR rises from 10.61% to 13.33%. The lower overall Macro-F1 cannot be interpreted entirely as forgetting: a new class with low F1 also enters the average.
Derivation and interpretation: docs/research/20261002/exp70_results.md and docs/slides/kor/1002_operational_qa/fixed_old_class_check.json.
notes.5:
This is not a model confusion matrix. Each cell is the fraction of rows in the original row class whose exact feature vector also occurs with the column class label.
Denominators are full class counts before cleaning. Percentages can be asymmetric because class sizes differ.
A row can share its feature vector with several labels and appear in several cells, so row sums are not removal rates.
Web attack: 1,335 rows overlap only with Benign, 3 only with Infiltration, 429 with both, and 771 with neither. The union contains 1,767 rows.
Rows and columns are sorted by full class counts before cleaning.
Data: docs/slides/kor/1002_intro_assets/*_pair_percent.csv and provenance.json. English figures use the same numeric matrices.
Conflicting labels are observed facts; window-based labeling is not assumed to cause every conflict.
notes.6:
Before and after counts cover the full train + validation + test data. The test column is a subset and must not be added to the after-cleaning total.
Sources: the cleaned split class_counts.csv and EXP61 global_raw per-class support.
Rows are sorted by full class counts after cleaning. Counts are unchanged from the Korean deck.
Tail refers to scarcity in the fixed test distribution, separate from context allocations. No arbitrary tail threshold is introduced.
notes.7:
The current implementation separates Global, Expert and Route pools. Experts use shared anchors plus residual-cluster blocks, and scorer/verifier models are trained separately.
Residual information includes input representations, Global probabilities, differences from the true label and error magnitude. Residual contexts are not necessarily limited to Global mistakes.
A frozen TabPFN backbone does not imply that S/V can also be updated without training.
The scorer selects an expert and decides whether to call it; the verifier decides whether to accept its prediction. Otherwise, the Global prediction is retained.
EXP70 compares updates of XGBoost and Global TabPFN as a foundation for this architecture. Update rules and costs for the complete expert/S/V model remain a separate evaluation.
notes.8:
Static EXP61/EXP63 results are preserved, with K=4 as the representative complete-model setting. EXP70 Global results do not replace the expert/S/V model result.
The complete proposed model uses additional labels from Expert and Route pools; this is not a claim of superiority under an identical 100,000-row information budget.
Global and DistPFN use the v3 backbone. BoostPFN and LoCalPFN use v1, and LoCalPFN includes fine-tuning.
The SOTA table reports the current static performance level. It does not replace the research objective with a competition for average F1.
Cost measurement conditions are reported on the next slide.
Sources: docs/research/20260930/exp61_report_data.json and exp63_capability_report_data.json.
notes.9:
EXP61 fit, inference and GPU measurements are preserved. Up to two concurrent jobs shared the GPU, so these are not standalone latency ratios.
GPU usage is the maximum per-process measurement sampled at one-second intervals.
LoCalPFN fit includes validation and inference includes retrieval. DistPFN includes shared Global computation and prior correction.
For the full model, expert predictions were prepared offline and the routing policy was evaluated afterward. Actual conditional runtime has not been measured. The ToN 100% call rate refers to one selected expert per sample, not all four.
TabPFN fit/setup includes preprocessing and cache construction without backbone retraining.
Do not treat EXP61 concurrent-job timings and EXP70 sequential-GPU timings as identical measurement conditions.
Source: docs/research/20260930/exp61_report_data.json.
notes.10:
The objective is to assess how effectively newly labeled attacks can be incorporated into an IDS, while preserving existing detection at an acceptable update and inference cost.
EXP70 gives a higher final Macro-F1 for TabPFN on CIC2018 and for XGBoost on ToN. XGBoost has shorter fit and inference times on both datasets in the current 100,000-row batch setting.
Not retraining backbone weights does not automatically yield lower operational cost.
Next, vary benign-example diversity and context size while measuring new attack recall, false positives and computational cost together. These are hypotheses for further evaluation, not improvements already demonstrated by EXP70.
Training and updates of experts and S/V must also be included when evaluating the full system.
F1 is one measure of utility. Recognizing unlabeled unknown attacks is a separate later OOD extension.
